Package com.workshop.mcp.spec

Record Class InputRequiredResult

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.workshop.mcp.spec.InputRequiredResult
Record Components:
resultType - always ResultType.INPUT_REQUIRED
inputRequests - the embedded requests, keyed by server-chosen identifiers that the responses come back under
requestState - opaque continuation state, echoed back byte-exact
public record InputRequiredResult(String resultType, Map<String,InputRequest> inputRequests, String requestState) extends Record
An interim result asking the client for information the server needs before it can finish the request.

This is the Multi Round-Trip Requests pattern. Instead of the server calling the client — impossible in revision 2026-07-28, where clients drop inbound requests — the server answers with what it still needs. The client gathers the answers and re-sends the original request, as a brand new request with a brand new id, carrying inputResponses and the requestState echoed back verbatim.

requestState is an opaque string, not JSON. It exists because the server has nowhere else to keep continuation state: sessions are gone, so anything the server learned while producing this interim result has to travel to the client and back. Conventionally it is base64-encoded JSON, but the protocol only guarantees the client returns the exact bytes.

At least one of inputRequests and requestState must be present. Servers may only return this from tools/call, prompts/get, and resources/read.

Since:
1.0
